reason: Both pages are accurate against facts.md: A's step 4 and 5 bills (4.05c vs 5c vs 6.62c, break-evens 0.11c and 13.3c) and B's monthly figures ($405 vs $500 vs $662 at $0.05, $4,030/$4,287 at $0.50, break-evens $0.0011 and $0.133) all recompute correctly. B fits finance managers better. Its calculator turns the GPT price into a monthly bill at a volume the reader types in. It splits each bar into the measured cheap-model-and-check cost and the expensive calls at your price. It writes a plain verdict sentence ('ask-twice is cheapest: $405 a month, $95 less...'), adds price presets including both break-evens, and ends with a clear 'Before you rely on this' list. A is a tidy six-step lesson with a good 14-of-72 dot sequence, and it shows the Wilson 12-30% interval that B leaves out. But its key slider step packs a log-scale share-of-bill chart and cent prices into very small type, which is harder for this audience to read. B's step 5 layout overflows at phone width, a real defect, but it does not outweigh B's clearer price-to-decision payoff.

A: Chart text in steps 4-6 (axis ticks, break-even labels, 'most saved: 19%', bill rows) is about 10-11 px at 390 px width and hard to read; the 'most saved' label sits on the 80% gridline
Step 5 explains cost as 'bill as a share of GPT on every invoice' on a log scale in cents per call, which is more abstract than a dollar bill for finance managers, and there is no volume input
The legend at the bottom of every step shows greyed-out entries, and the step cards leave large empty gaps above the controls, so the controls sit far from the content
B: At 390 px, step 5 ('Does the saving cover the cost of checking?') overflows its card (story-text and story-vis span -7 to 409 px): the right column of the invoice grid and the 'Try a price' button are clipped
The monthly-saving line chart's labels (axis ticks, 'break-even $0.0011', 'break-even $0.133') are about 8 px and unreadable at phone width

The 19.4% cheap-model accuracy has no uncertainty interval (facts give Wilson 12-30% on 72 invoices). Step 2's 'about $0.00014 per invoice' for one cheap call also sits oddly beside $0.000218 for two calls
